canonical_topic: Real options: using options theory to analyze discretionary investments
definition: Investment decisions that involve a choice about whether to act (rather than an obligation to act) can be modeled using option theory, because the decision-maker retains the right, not the requirement, to proceed.
core_idea: Building a power plant effectively hands the operator an option to convert fuel into electricity, exercised only when doing so is profitable, so option analysis is a natural framework for this and similar discretionary investments.
key_points: A power plant gives its operator the choice, not the obligation, to burn fuel and produce electricity.
The operator only 'exercises' by running the plant when production is profitable.
Any investment decision with embedded discretion can be analyzed using option logic.
trading_implications: Physical assets with dispatch flexibility can be valued using option-pricing style frameworks rather than a single static NPV estimate.
